speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your neck swelling, can you tell me how long you have noticed it and if it has been growing in size? Also, does the swelling move up when you swallow or stick out your tongue?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the location on the nape of the neck and your history of colon cancer, I need to rule out metastasis or an epidermoid cyst. Does the swelling feel firm or soft, and is it mobile or fixed to the underlying tissues? REQUEST TEST: Fine_Needle_Aspiration_Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the FNA was non-diagnostic, let's look closer at the skin changes. Is the overlying skin thickened, nodular, or "peau d'orange" in appearance? REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Colon cancer (colectomy performed), type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, osteoarthritis of the left knee. Social history: Works as a traffic warden, frequently plays golf.

speaker: Doctor
text: The FNA was non-diagnostic, which is unusual for a metastatic deposit or a simple cyst, so we need to visualize the internal structure. REQUEST TEST: MRI of the neck
